rows.scope: CXS 193-1995 Arsenic table: 'Edible fats and oils' ML 0.1 mg/kg, 'Whole commodity', remark 'The relevant Codex commodity standards are CXS 19-1981, CXS 33-1981, CXS 210-1999, CXS 211-1999 and CXS 329-2017'; CXS 210-1999 §5 Contaminants: 'shall comply with the maximum levels of the General Standard for Contaminants and Toxins in Food and Feed (CXS 193-1995)'
rows.basis: whole commodity; total arsenic (As-tot) 'when not otherwise mentioned' (fish oils under CXS 329 are As-in)
rows.evidence: 'Edible fats and oils 0.1 Whole commodity' — CXS 193-1995 Arsenic ML table (held copy 'Adopted in 1995, last amended in 2025', PDF p.56); CXS 210-1999 §5 (2015 ed. fao.org p.4; 2019-amended ed. mirror p.6)
rows.primary_source_used: raw/regulatory/codex/codex-cxs-193-1995-current-2025.pdf (numeric ML); https://www.fao.org/input/download/standards/336/CXS_210e_2015.pdf (CXS 210 §5, 2015 edition, HTTP 200); https://oleina.ua/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/Codex-Alimentarius.pdf (CXS 210 2019-amended edition, mirror); https://www.fao.org/input/download/standards/74/CXS_019e_2015.pdf (CXS 19 §4, 2015 edition)
rows.note: Value 0.1 mg/kg tAs = 100 ug/kg for edible fats and oils covering named vegetable oils: MATCH on value, scope and basis. Provenance caveats for the register note: (1) neither CXS 210-1999 §5 nor CXS 19-1981 §4 carries its own numeric heavy-metal table in any edition I could read (2015 from fao.org; 2019-amended via mirror); both defer to CXS 193, which is where the 0.1 mg/kg As ML lives with CXS 210/CXS 19 named as the relevant commodity standards; (2) the CXS 193 lead ML for edible fats and oils is 0.08 mg/kg ('whole commodity as prepared for wholesale or retail distribution'), not 0.1; (3) the CCFO-to-CCCF consolidation the note describes as pending is already reflected in CXS 193. Current-edition CXS 210 PDF and the Codex list page on fao.org returned HTTP 403 to fetch and a Cloudflare 'verify you are human' check in the browser, which I did not click; the CXS 210 edition years quoted are therefore 'Adopted 1999; revised 2001, 2003, 2009, 2017, 2019; amended 2005, 2011, 2013, 2015, 2019' from the mirror, and post-2019 revisions of CXS 210 could not be read. CXS 193 currency is from the held 2025 copy.

rows.scope: 表 A.1 entry 硫酸铝钾(又名钾明矾),硫酸铝铵(又名铵明矾) INS 522, 523 (膨松剂、稳定剂): 07.0 焙烤食品 (Annex E: 07.01 面包, 07.02 糕点, 07.03 饼干), 06.03.02.05 油炸面制品, 06.11 面糊(如用于鱼和禽肉的拖面糊)、裹粉、煎炸粉 — each 按生产需要适量使用 with 备注 铝的残留量≤100 mg/kg(干样品,以 Al 计)
rows.basis: 干样品,以 Al 计 (dry sample, calculated as Al); residue limit for the permitted aluminium additives
rows.evidence: '07.0 焙烤食品 按生产需要适量使用 铝的残留量≤100 mg/kg(干样品,以 Al 计)' — GB 2760-2024 表 A.1(续) p.77 (PDF p.80)
rows.primary_source_used: http://gdgrain.gd.gov.cn/attachment/0/561/561845/4506199.pdf (official GB 2760-2024 text, 264 pp., hosted by Guangdong provincial government; cover '2024-02-08 发布 2025-02-08 实施', '本标准代替 GB 2760-2014'); register URL chinesestandard.net returned HTTP 403
rows.note: 100 mg/kg = 100000 ug/kg for all three row scopes (baked foods 07.0 incl. bread/pastries/cakes/biscuits-crackers-cookies under 07.01-07.03; deep-fried flour products 06.03.02.05; batter/breading/frying powder 06.11). In force since 2025-02-08, replacing GB 2760-2014; no held copy in raw/regulatory. Caveats: this is an additive-use residue cap (铝的残留量) in a food-additive standard, not a contaminant ML, so 'maximum level' status should be read as such; sibling entries differ (粉丝、粉条 06.05.02.01 200 mg/kg dry; 腌制水产品(仅限海蜇) 09.03.02 500 mg/kg in ready-to-eat jellyfish as Al); the batter/breading category code is 06.11 in the 2024 edition.
